name: The Notorious B.I.G.
hook: A Brooklyn rapper whose debut was steered from street records towards radio hits by Sean Combs, with one of its hardest tracks by DJ Premier, and whose murder in 1997 is still unsolved.
blurb: Christopher Wallace, the Notorious B.I.G. or Biggie Smalls, was born in Brooklyn on 21 May 1972 and grew up in Clinton Hill. Sean Combs heard his demo tape and signed him to Bad Boy Records in 1993. His first album, 'Ready to Die' (13 September 1994), recorded at the Hit Factory and D&D Studios, mixed dark, detailed songs about crime and poverty from the early sessions with radio hits from the later ones, 'Juicy' (built on Mtume's 'Juicy Fruit') and 'Big Poppa', which Combs pushed him to make. DJ Premier produced 'Unbelievable', and Easy Mo Bee and others most of the rest. From 1995 he was caught up in a feud with his former friend Tupac Shakur, which grew into the centre of a rivalry between East Coast and West Coast rap. Tupac was shot dead in Las Vegas in September 1996. On 9 March 1997 Biggie was killed in a drive-by shooting in Los Angeles, aged 24. Nobody has been convicted of either killing. His second album, 'Life After Death', came out on 25 March 1997, two weeks after he died, and debuted at number one.
